Not acted on, for the reason given under VSA-13: the repair records under rewrite/spec/conflicts/ are history and are not corrected after the fact. The fixes they claim are tracked in this ledger under their own ids (AU-S2-04, -08, -10, -11, -14).

The retirement of BLUEPRINT.md#11.3 now names the sections that hold the text (hooks.md#2.11.10, pipeline.md#2.9.8, pipeline.md#2.8) and the three spec files that carry it.

Applied during C2 and its fix pass, checked by the orchestrating session: the story.js skeleton in topics/story-script.md holds no KIND copy and reads tests_agent, tests_method, impl_agent and impl_method from the unit, and story-unit.schema.json defines and requires those names. W2 is built from that skeleton.

For the story-ready fixture (E1's part of thin-slice step 6): state in packaging/sample-project.md, and write in the loader, the values with and without --local: with --local, delivery.mode is local and delivery.ci is none; without it, delivery.mode is pr and delivery.ci is what the overlay names. A unit test loads the overlay both ways and validates it.

Accepted at slice depth, where the seven shipped kinds are exactly the story path and the lint failing loudly is the intent. For each agent package that widens a method set (A4 first): update the need rows of the L-KIND check in the same change; if a third reader of the need table appears, move it into a shipped table and have the lint and the build read that.

For A1 (the agent frame) and every agent package that writes a tools line holding an MCP tool name: write the value quoted (tools: "Read, mcp__..."), because the shipped frontmatter reader refuses a bare scalar with an underscore, and correct the unquoted examples in topics/research-and-browser-tools.md and topics/agent-file.md in the same change. The agent lint already fails a file the reader refuses, so a miss is loud. Given to the step 5 build in its launch notes.

For H3, which builds the read walls: when [reveals] is generated from the kind classes, emit one entry per listable kind whose class any caller is denied, adding list project-conventions = ["guidance"], with a test that a code-reviewer may list project conventions.

For W2 (and W3 for the holdout members): type the members of survey.config that a script reads in survey.schema.json (tier_override and review_rules as strings; holdout as an object with its three numeric thresholds) and require them, empty where the project has none, so that the prelude's empty form and the fixtures carry them; run tools/build.py in the same step. Given to the step 6 build of the story workflow in its launch notes.

For B5 when the harness is next changed: give harness.mjs a helper that stamps workflow-lib/prelude.js between the markers of a workflow body written in a temporary directory, and have the identity test use it, so that a test author writes bodies only.

For the first headless run (E2's part of thin-slice step 6) and every later unattended run: the driver creates its project under a directory outside Claude Code's own temporary tree (under $HOME by default, with a switch), and nothing the run needs travels only in a project CLAUDE.md: the SessionStart briefing and the survey carry it. For K1's setup skill: say the same where it writes the project CLAUDE.md sections. Given to the step 6 build in its launch notes.

For A3 (the agents that read a local fixture) and E1 (the wall probes): a localhost fixture is reached through the shell (curl), where the walls already apply, never through WebFetch, which refuses an undotted host and upgrades 127.0.0.1 to HTTPS; the wall probe verifies the shell route.
